query: What are the main types of concerns patients come in with in these visit notes?

per_column.name: primary_concern
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by categorizing the type of patient concern into an actionable grouping axis. Most samples are well-grounded (knee pain->MSK, MI follow-up->Cardiac, acne->Skin). However the annual physical exam row was misclassified as 'Respiratory/Cough' despite the text being a routine physical with mild fatigue and no respiratory complaint, indicating some ungrounded assignment.

per_column.name: concern_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a coarser, complementary grouping (chronic vs acute vs infectious) that adds a distinct analytical axis beyond primary_concern. Grounded on most samples (MI->Chronic, injury->Acute Injury/Trauma). The annual physical exam labeled 'Infectious Disease' is unsupported by the text. Note the value set mixes taxonomies (some rows carry Skin/Neurological/GI labels identical to primary_concern), slightly reducing coherence but still usable.

per_column.name: visit_severity
per_column.rationale: A severity axis is useful for grouping but partly overlaps with the existing 'urgency' original column; the samples track urgency closely (Urgent->Acute/Urgent, Routine->Routine/Chronic), making it somewhat redundant though it adds a chronic-vs-critical distinction. Values shown are well-grounded in the source text.

per_column.name: primary_concern.1
per_column.rationale: An exact duplicate of primary_concern with identical value distribution and identical row-level outputs; adds no new analytical leverage. Groundedness mirrors the original but redundancy makes it near-useless.

per_column.name: concern_category.1
per_column.rationale: Exact duplicate of concern_category with identical distribution and row values; trivially redundant and provides no additional axis.

per_column.name: visit_severity.1
per_column.rationale: Exact duplicate of visit_severity; no new information. Values grounded but redundant.

judge.rationale: The first three columns give genuinely useful, largely well-grounded axes (concern type, category, severity) that directly serve the query, though visit_severity overlaps with the existing urgency column and there is a clear misclassification of the routine physical row as respiratory/infectious. The latter three columns are exact duplicates that add no analytical value, which drags the holistic usefulness down considerably. Groundedness is generally solid across samples with occasional unsupported assignments.
